result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.dfs_predecessors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Map every node reached by a depth-first search to its parent. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47919-L47975){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.dfs_predecessors( source=None, depth_limit=None, mode="out", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![DFS predecessors](/assets/graphs/dfs-predecessors.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A four-node tree searched depth-first from A (outlined): A joins B and D, and B joins C. The search runs A, B, C before backing up to D, as the numbered badges show, and each accent arrow points from a node back to its parent. The card maps B to A, C to B, and D to A." width="100%"} The depth-first search tree (or forest, when no source is given) assigns each reached node the node it was discovered from. Depth-first trees are the basis of many structural algorithms (bridges, articulation points, strongly connected components), and this dictionary is their parent array. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional start node (ID or label). If `None` (default), every component is searched, starting from the lowest node ID. [depth_limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional maximum depth. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge direction to follow on directed graphs: `"out"` (default), `"in"` or `"all"`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Child node ID to parent node ID (roots are not keys). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the source does not exist or `mode` is invalid. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Read off the tree edges of `dfs_edges()`. Matches NetworkX's `dfs_predecessors`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#22ac3223 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("A", "D")]) {g.get_label_from_id(c): g.get_label_from_id(p) for c, p in g.dfs_predecessors("A").items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'B': 'A', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'A'} ``` ::: :::
